senses.definition: A person or thing that translates meaning from one language into another, particularly

subsenses.definition: A person or thing that translates various forms of text.
(inexact, sometimes proscribed) Synonym of interpreter, a person or thing that immediately interprets direct speech.

quotes.text:
"You don't believe the Soviet Union is going to reduce its defense budget, do you?" Boggs asked.
Premier Chou didn't wait for the translator to finish. "Never, never, never," he replied in perfect English.
quotes.reference: 1980, Gerald Ford, “Boyhood—and Beyond”, in A Time to Heal, New York: Berkley Books, →ISBN, page 95:

subsenses.definition: (figuratively) A person or thing that expresses an idea or style in a new form or medium.

quotes.text: Mr. C. Blair Leighton... lithographer... was one of the earliest translators of water and oil pictures by the chromatic process.

subsenses.definition: (computing, chiefly historical) A machine that converts inputs into a pattern of holes on a punch card.
(chiefly US) A relay station that retransmits incoming television signals after automatically adjusting their frequency to avoid interference.
(computing) A program that converts commands from one computer language into another.

senses.definition: (chiefly obsolete) Synonym of carrier, a person who transports something, now particularly (Roman Catholicism, rare) holy relics.

quotes.text: ... the translator of the life and miracles of the saints, like the translator of the relics, need not have been "literate"; nor did he have to be a clerk.

senses.definition: (historical) Synonym of repairer, particularly of leather or cloth goods.

quotes.text: Boots and Shoes are not to be had, I am told, in sufficient quantity for the demand from the slop-shops, the "translators," and the second-hand dealers. Great quantities of second-hand boots and shoes are sent to Ireland to be "translated" there.
quotes.reference: 1851, Henry Mayhew, London Labour and the London Poor, page 33:

synonyms: particularly of leather or cloth goods

senses.definition: (historical, slang) A used and repaired shoe, boot, or other item of clothing.
(obsolete) Synonym of repeater, a thing that automatically retransmits an incoming message along a telegraph line.
(obsolete) A thing that converts energy from one form to another.
